proof:
# A strict-quota compatible square pyramid with no affine face section

This exact obstruction rules out supplying the affine center graph in the
exposed-face contraction theorem from compatibility and strict closed-minor
quotas alone. It has arbitrary positive convex planar fibers and an already
canonical complete lattice base. It is NOT asserted to be a critical family,
a joint bad minimum, or an OC counterexample.

## 1. Complete base and actual positive fibers

In Z^3 put

    a=(1,0,0), b=(-1,0,0), c=(0,1,0), d=(0,-1,0),
    o=(0,0,0), m=(0,0,1), t=(0,0,2),
    P={a,b,c,d,o,m,t}.

The convex hull B is the square pyramid

    0<=z<=2,       |x|+|y|<=1-z/2.

Its integer slices are exactly {a,b,c,d,o} at height zero, {m} at height
one, and {t} at height two. Thus P is lattice-complete. Its four occupied
parities are those of a,b; of c,d; of o,t; and of m. The proper bottom
face F={z=0} is a quadrilateral, not a simplex.

Let S_s=[-s/2,s/2]^2 be the planar square of side s, and put

    D=203/220,       e=(D,0),       g=(D/2,0).

Choose the vertex fibers

    K_a=S_1,        K_b=S_(1/10),
    K_c=e+S_1,      K_d=e+S_(1/10).

Their opposite-pair midpoint bodies are

    A=(K_a+K_b)/2=S_(11/20),
    C=(K_c+K_d)/2=e+S_(11/20).                              (1)

Their convex hull is the rectangle

    K_o=conv(A union C)
       =[-11/40, D+11/40] times [-11/40,11/40].             (2)

It is centered at g and has width 81/55 and height 11/20. Finally set

    K_t=g+(4/5)(K_o-g),
    K_m=g+(9/10)(K_o-g)=(K_o+K_t)/2.                       (3)

All seven fibers are positive compact planar convex bodies.

These are exactly the integer fibers of the actual convex hull of the
five vertex fibers at a,b,c,d,t. To see this at o, every bottom-base
representation of zero has equal coefficients on a,b and equal coefficients
on c,d. Its fiber combination is a convex combination of the two sets
in (1), giving exactly (2). At m, every representation has weight 1/2
on t and a bottom-base combination of mean zero with the remaining
weight 1/2. Its fiber is exactly (K_t+K_o)/2, as in (3). All other sampled
bases are vertices. Consequently EVERY anchored Minkowski inclusion holds,
not merely the displayed midpoint inclusions. There are no additional
integer bases. The ambient convex hull has interior in R^(3+2).

In particular the actual volume-root data V_z^(1/2) are compatible concave.
This extra geometric condition does not remedy the obstruction below.

## 2. Every proper closed-minor quota is strict

The exact volumes, in the displayed order, are

    (V_a,V_b,V_c,V_d,V_o,V_m,V_t)
      =(1,1/100,1,1/100,81/100,6561/10000,324/625),

and

    M=8009/2000,       M/k=8009/8000.                        (4)

Here is a complete elementary closed-minor certificate. A subset T of P
is closed exactly when it is stable under

    {a,b} -> o,       {c,d} -> o,       {o,t} -> m.            (5)

Indeed only o and m can be newly created in a convex hull of omitted
points, because all other points are vertices. The bottom mean-zero
representations described in Section 1 prove that o is created precisely
by an opposite pair. To create m requires t with weight 1/2 and a
bottom mean-zero combination, hence o or an opposite pair. These are
exactly the closure consequences of (5).

Among the 126 nonempty proper subsets, precisely 82 obey (5). For ALL
82 the rational arithmetic gives

    k(T) M/4 - V(T)>0,
    min_(proper nonempty closed T) [k(T)M/4-V(T)]=9/8000.     (6)

The minimum is attained by either unit-area singleton a or c. The
standalone verifier enumerates every subset, applies only the three
proved closure rules, and checks each fraction exactly. Thus (6) is a
complete certificate, not a numerical feasibility assertion.

## 3. The affine-center polytope is empty

Suppose an affine map s:F->R^2 selected a point of every actual fiber,
s(z) in K_z. The two diagonal relations in the bottom quadrilateral force

    s(o)=[s(a)+s(b)]/2=[s(c)+s(d)]/2.

By (1), the first value lies in A and the second in C. But A and C are
disjoint: the horizontal distance between their centers is 203/220,
whereas their common side length is 11/20=121/220. Their separating
horizontal gap is exactly

    D-11/20=41/110>0.                                       (7)

This is impossible. Hence there is no affine section, even allowing
boundary selections. In particular there are no affine interior centers
for a simultaneous homothety of this nonsimplex face.

The obstruction is the actual affine dependence at the face, not a
failure to choose the right centroids or representation. Picking one
minimal anchored representation at o ignores the incompatible second
one. An actual affine map has to obey both.

## 4. Canonical representation-preserving lifting does not repair it

A scalar function h on P preserving all anchored affine representations
must in particular satisfy

    h(a)+h(b)=2h(o),       h(c)+h(d)=2h(o),
    h(t)+h(o)=2h(m).                                        (8)

These three independent equations leave dimension four. They force

    h(x,y,z)=h(o)+A x+B y+C z

on P. Conversely every such ordinary affine function preserves all
anchored representations. The full representation-preserving function
space is therefore EXACTLY the ordinary four-dimensional affine space.

The base is already canonical up to an affine isomorphism. A canonical
lift using this whole function space cannot increase its affine rank
or remove the bottom diagonal relation. More generally every coordinate
of any representation-preserving lift is affine on this example. A
faithful full-rank such lift retains the quadrilateral and the same
incompatibility (7). No unproved invariance of mixed depth under an
arbitrary nonaffine change of base is being used.

## 5. Scope and remaining joint-minimum question

This family simultaneously has lattice completeness, full base rank,
positive actual convex fibers, compatible square-root volumes, and all
strict proper closed-minor quotas. Those premises alone do not imply
coherent affine center maps on an arbitrary exposed face.

The example does not specify any critical buffered menu or claim that
this face is populated by maximizing atomic marks. A theorem deriving an
affine selection at a JOINT bad minimum would therefore need genuinely
additional depth, equality or variational information. The simplex-face
hypothesis in the proved atomic plateau descent cannot be dropped using
only quotas, compatibility, or canonical lifting.
